summary: Portugal is part of the Schengen Area: EU and EFTA citizens enter freely, nationals of the 63 countries and territories on the EU's visa-exempt list (as of 30 December 2025) can stay 90 days in any 180-day period (the ETIAS travel authorization is not yet in operation), and everyone else needs a Schengen short-stay visa (general fee €90). Long-stay options include residency visas for people living from passive income and for digital nomads working remotely.

tips.text: The 90-day limit counts across the entire Schengen Area, not just Portugal — days spent in Spain or France count against the same allowance.
The Government of Canada says pickpocketing and bag snatching are common in Lisbon and Porto, and advises extra caution on Lisbon's trams 15, 25 and 28.
The Government of Canada says most highways in Portugal require tolls, that you may need to pay electronically, and that international credit or debit cards are not always accepted.
The official ETIAS website, travel-europe.europa.eu, gives the fee as EUR 20 when you apply through it; applicants under 18 or over 70 are exempt from paying.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Portugal?
faq.answer: No. US passport holders can visit Portugal and the rest of the Schengen Area visa-free for up to 90 days in any 180-day period. Once ETIAS starts, they will need to obtain this online authorization (€20) before travel.

faq.question: How much does a Portugal Schengen visa cost?
faq.answer: The general Schengen short-stay visa fee is €90 for adults and €45 for children aged 6–11. It allows stays of up to 90 days in any 180-day period across all Schengen countries.

faq.question: What income do I need for Portugal's residency visa for people living from passive income?
faq.answer: This visa requires stable passive income (pension, rents, dividends) of at least the Portuguese minimum wage — €920 per month in 2026. The visa fee is €110 and the visa leads to a residence permit.

faq.question: Does Portugal have a digital nomad visa?
faq.answer: Yes. The residency visa for remote professional activity is for remote workers employed by companies outside Portugal. You must show average monthly income of four times the Portuguese minimum wage — €3,680 per month in 2026 — over the last three months. The visa fee is €110.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Portugal without a visa?
faq.answer: Visa-exempt non-EU visitors can stay up to 90 days within any 180-day period, counted across the whole Schengen Area. EU and EFTA citizens do not need a visa.
